{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjccM8AAAABZYkP2Q", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IfzhC_5zA", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3If", "number": 21, "title": "Implement internal EEPROM transfers, settings protection and console persistence", "body": "## Problem

At main `ea784e2504d73873a2546c59933666817509d274`, `Bus::input/output` rejects internal EEPROM ports BA–BE. The existing EEPROM controller and save APIs support cartridge storage only. Ordinary software cannot read owner settings or exchange data through the console's shared software area.

`Machine::load_rom`, restart and model changes reconstruct the bus; adding storage there without retention would lose console data. Browser persistence currently uses cartridge ROM identities only.

## Expected outcome

Implement ordinary internal EEPROM READ, WRITE and write-enable/disable operations, settings protection and separate console persistence for WonderSwan, WonderSwan Color and SwanCrystal. Preserve 128 bytes on Mono and 2048 bytes on each Color model, including when Color hardware runs in mono mode.

Bound this milestone to ordinary word transfers and retention. Direct ERASE, WRAL/ERAL and unresolved silicon edge cases remain explicit hardware gaps; do not inherit cartridge behavior or claim complete EEPROM accuracy. No settings-editor UI or broader firmware implementation is required.

## Context

Relevant paths: `crates/ws-core/src/{bus,eeprom,cartridge,lib}.rs`, `crates/ws-web/src/lib.rs`, `web/src/{saves,main}.ts`, existing fixture tooling and browser compatibility tests.

Inspected [libws definitions](https://wonderful.asie.pl/doc/libws/eeprom_8h_source.html) describe capacities, the 96-byte software area and owner/settings locations. Its [current source header](https://github.com/WonderfulToolchain/target-wswan-syslibs/blob/main/libws/include/ws/eeprom.h) documents protection of byte addresses 0x60 upward and the cartridge-header exception. [Register definitions](https://wonderful.asie.pl/doc/libws/ports_8h_source.html) specify BA/BC/BE and control/status bits.

Planning correction: a capacity-only reuse of the cartridge controller would be incorrect. Internal BE bit 7 sets protection; external C8 bit 7 aborts. Command width follows active mono/Color mode, as shown by [libws](https://github.com/WonderfulToolchain/target-wswan-syslibs/blob/main/libws/src/eeprom/eeprom_handle_internal.c). Separate these requirements from cartridge-controller quirks.

The public [internal EEPROM test](https://github.com/asiekierka/ws-test-suite/blob/main/src/mono/eeprom/internal/main.c) supplies buffer, status, locking, protection and mode-transition vectors. It explicitly marks direct erase behavior uncertain and substitutes WRITE FFFF. This is inspected experiment source, not a reported hardware pass. Ares also labels protection/command-adaptation edge cases as guesses. WSdev rendered/raw references were inaccessible; their search excerpts establish no requirements.

PR #20 and `docs/issue-19-validation.md` report 69 core unit tests, seven integration tests and both Chromium suites passing. Existing EEPROM tests cover cartridge storage, not internal storage. No checks were rerun during planning; the Pages workflow contains builds/deployment but no hardware tests.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Implement BA/BB data, BC/BD command and BE control/status, separate read/write buffers, READ/WRITE and write-enable/disable flows. Support byte I/O and the word I/O used by libws, including harmless BF high-byte accesses with a documented reserved-byte policy.
- [ ] Test independent 128/2048-byte capacities, boundary words, little-endian data, six-bit mono and ten-bit Color command formats, and Color/Crystal mono↔Color transitions without reallocating or erasing storage.
- [ ] Implement BE protection/readback: software bytes 00–5F remain writable while settings at 60 upward reject writes. Test boundary words 5E/60, write locking, repeated protection and protection across mode changes. Apply the existing header protection flag through an explicitly documented firmware-free handoff policy on load/restart, without synthesizing unrelated firmware services.
- [ ] Use shared emulated clocks for bounded completion. Test READ DONE clearing then completing, READY progression, unchanged read buffers during writes, captured pending operands and continued timer/audio/DMA progress. Document approximate latency separately from measured timing; unsupported commands must remain identifiable and leave storage unchanged.
- [ ] Add length-checked core/Wasm console-data import/export independent of cartridge saves. Completed bytes survive restart, reset/unload, cartridge replacement and switching away from and back to a model. Failed imports, incompatible model changes and invalid ROM loads preserve existing data. Document deterministic synthetic initial settings without claiming factory-image accuracy.
- [ ] Persist separate versioned console records per model across browser reload/reopen and across different cartridges. Restore before execution and flush before lifecycle/model replacement. Preserve unreadable existing records; unavailable/full storage must report failure without corrupting cartridge saves or stopping emulation. Console data stays browser-local.
- [ ] Add original CC0 CPU-driven probes for settings reads, shared-area writes, status polling, locking and protection on all three models. Native tests and the existing production-preview Chromium compatibility suite must demonstrate cross-cartridge retention, model isolation, reload/reopen and storage-failure handling through actual Wasm execution.
- [ ] Coordinator runs and records `python3 fixtures/build.py --check`, `python3 demo/build.py --check`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, and `git diff --check`; in `web`, run `npm run build:wasm`, `npm run build`, `npm run test:browser` and `npm run test:compat` against production preview. Preserve existing three-model gameplay, audio, GDMA/SDMA, SRAM/external EEPROM, firmware-free startup and browser lifecycle coverage.
- [ ] Update support/API documentation and provenance. Record unresolved direct erase/bulk operations and timing limits honestly. Coordinator completes source-Issue review and resolves blocking findings before merge; retain the from-scratch core and thin Wasm adapter without proprietary software or title-specific behavior.

## Optional validation

Compare additional publicly documented hardware vectors or appropriately licensed independent software. Physical-console access, commercial ROMs and human gameplay are unnecessary for mandatory acceptance. Report optional checks only if performed.

## Required post-merge verification

None.

## Specification reconciliation

This task was authored by AI under the agreed WonderSwan-family hardware goal.
Correct erroneous technical assumptions or acceptance criteria when primary hardware
specifications establish the correction. Update this Issue and record the original
assumption, corrected requirement, primary reference and rationale in the PR.
These technical corrections require neither human approval nor an independent AI
re-review. Preserve the agreed goal and relevant pre-merge acceptance; do not weaken
requirements merely to accommodate incomplete implementation or failing tests.
